questions.question: A shopkeeper sold a pair of headphones for Rs. 5,520 at a gain of 20%. What would have been the gain or loss percent if it had been sold for Rs. 4,370?
questions.solution:
**Given:- **

 

A shopkeeper sold a pair of headphones for Rs. 5,520 at a gain of 20%.

**Formula used:-**

Gain percent= [(Selling Price−Cost Price) ​ ×100]/Cost price 

Loss percent= [(Cost Price - Selling Price) ​ ×100]/Cost price 

**Calculation:-**

 SP = CP + Gain 5520 

⇒ 5520 = CP + (20 × CP)/100 

⇒ (120/100 CP) = 5520 ​ 

 

⇒ CP = 4600 

 Loss percent = [( 4600− 4370 )/4600] × 100 

⇒ ( 230/4600) × 100 = 5% 

**∴ If the headphones were sold for Rs. 4,370, there would be a loss of 5%. **

An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 120 hours while an outlet pipe drains a completely-filled tank in 54 hours. If 8 inlet pipes and 3 outlet pipes are opened simultaneously, when the tank is empty, then in how many hours will the tank get completely filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 120 and 54) = 1080 units.

Efficiency of 1 inlet pipe = 1080 ÷ 120 = +9 units/hr.

Efficiency of 1 outlet pipe = 1080 ÷ (−54) = −20 units/hr.

Net efficiency of (8 inlets + 3 outlets) = (8 × 9) + (3 × −20) = 72 − 60 = +12 units/hr.

Time required to fill tank = 1080 ÷ 12 = 90 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by 1 inlet pipe to fill the tank = 120 hours

⇒ Time taken by 1 outlet pipe to empty the tank = 54 hours

⇒ Number of inlet pipes opened = 8

⇒ Number of outlet pipes opened = 3

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

⇒ Total Time = Total Work ÷ Net Combined Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 1 Inlet Pipe

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of 8 inlet pipes = 8 × (+9) = +72 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of 3 outlet pipes = 3 × (−20) = −60 units/hour

⇒ Net combined efficiency when both types are opened together = +72 − 60 = +12 units/hour

⇒ The positive sign indicates that the tank is being filled.

⇒ Total time required to completely fill the tank = 1080 ÷ 12

⇒ Total time = 90 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 90 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours and an outlet pipe empties it in y hours, the net part of the tank filled in 1 hour is given by (1/x − 1/y).

Efficiency Approach (LCM Method)

Treat inlet pipes as positive work providers (filling) and outlet pipes as negative work providers (draining). The total capacity of the tank is considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their individual completion times.

Multiple Similar Pipes

When multiple pipes of the same capacity operate simultaneously, simply multiply the individual pipe's efficiency by the total number of identical pipes before evaluating the net overall flow.

questions.question: The marked price of a frock is Rs. 4,500. It is to be sold at Rs. 2,400 at two successive discounts. If the first discount is 20%, then the second discount will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The marked price of a frock is Rs. 4,500. It is to be sold at Rs. 2,400 at two successive discounts

**Calculation:**

MP of the article = Rs. 4500

SP of the article after getting 20% discount = 4500 × (80/100) = 3600

Second SP of the article = Rs. 2400

Second discount = 3600 – 2400 = 1200

∴ Discount percentage = 1200/3600 × 100 = 100/3%

**∴ The correct option is 4**

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Divisibility rule of 11

This rule states that the given number can only be completely divided by 11 if the sum of digits at an odd position and the sum of digits at an even position in a number is 0 or 11.

(1) 97174

A sum of digits at even positions = 9 + 1 + 4 = 14

A sum of digits at odd positions = 7 + 7 = 14

Difference = 14 - 14 = 0

Since the difference is 0, 97174 is divisible by 11.

(2) 56923 

A sum of digits at even positions = 5 + 9 + 3 = 17

A sum of digits at odd positions = 6 + 2 = 8

Difference = 17 - 8 = 9

Since the difference is not a multiple of 11, 56923 is not divisible by 11.

(3) 63962 

A sum of digits at even positions = 3 + 6 = 9

A sum of digits at odd positions = 6 + 9 + 2 = 17

Difference = 17 - 9 = 8

Since the difference is not a multiple of 11, 63962 is not divisible by 11.

(4) 17295

A sum of digits at even positions = 1 + 2 + 5 = 8

A sum of digits at odd positions = 7 + 9 = 16

Difference = 16 - 8 = 8

Since the difference is not a multiple of 11, 17295 is not divisible by 11.

**∴The number that is divisible by 11 is__ 97174__.**

questions.question: Two trains of length 130 m and 120 m are running on parallel lines in the same direction at a speed of 40 km/h and 50 km/h, respectively. In how much time will they pass each other?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = Sum of train lengths = 130 + 120 = 250 m.

Relative speed in same direction = 50 − 40 = 10 km/h.

Convert speed to m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 25/9 m/s.

Time taken = Distance ÷ Speed = 250 × (9/25) = 90 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 Train 1 (130 m)
 
• 
 40 km/h
 
 
 Train 2 (120 m)
 
• 
 50 km/h
 
 
• 
 Total Dist = 250 m | Rel Speed = 10 km/h

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 130 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 120 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 40 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross = (Total Distance) ÷ (Relative Speed)

Total Distance = L₁ + L₂

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₂ − S₁

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 130 + 120 = 250 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 − 40 = 10 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 50/18 = 25/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 250 ÷ (25/9)

⇒ Time taken = (250 × 9) ÷ 25

⇒ Time taken = 10 × 9 = 90 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 90 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trains Running in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Crossing a Stationary Point

When a train crosses a vertical pole, a standing man or a signal post, the total distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train itself.

Unit Conversion Trick

To rapidly convert km/h to m/s, simply multiply the value by 5/18. Conversely, to change m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: The square of the sum of two given natural numbers is 784, while the product of the two given numbers is 192. Find the positive difference between the squares of these two given numbers.
questions.solution:
Let the numbers are X and Y

**Given:**

(X + Y)2 = 784 and XY = 192

Calculation:

(X + Y)2 = 784 ⇒ (X + Y) = 28

⇒ X² + Y² + 2XY = 784

⇒ X2 + Y2 + 2 × 192 = 784

⇒ X2 + Y2 = 400

So,

⇒ X2 + Y2 - 2XY = 400 - 2 × 192

⇒ X2 + Y2 - 2XY = 16

⇒ (X - Y)² = 16

⇒ X - Y = 4

Now,

X2 - Y2 = (X + Y)(X - Y)

⇒ 28 × 4 = 112

**∴ The correct option is 4**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**According to the question,

(x + y)2 = 784

⇒ x + y = √784 = 28

xy = 192

x - y = √{(x + y)2 - 4xy}

⇒ √{282 - 4 × 192} = √16 = 4

Now, x2 - y2 = (x + y)(x - y) = 28 × 4 = 112

A work for 65 /3 - 50/3 = 5 days

questions.question: A boat can go 60 km downstream and 40 km upstream in 12 hours 30 minutes. It can go 84 km downstream and 63 km upstream in 18 hours 54 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h, to the nearest integer) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide first case by 20: 3/D + 2/U = 0.625

Divide second case by 21: 4/D + 3/U = 0.90

Eliminate 1/D: 3 × (4/D + 3/U) − 4 × (3/D + 2/U) = 3(0.9) − 4(0.625)

1/U = 2.7 − 2.5 = 0.2 ⇒ Upstream speed (U) = 5 km/h

3/D + 2(0.2) = 0.625 ⇒ 3/D = 0.225 ⇒ Downstream speed (D) = 13.33 km/h

Boat speed = (13.33 + 5) ÷ 2 = 9.165 ≈ 9 km/h

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Distance downstream = 60 km, Distance upstream = 40 km, Time = 12.5 hours

Case 2: Distance downstream = 84 km, Distance upstream = 63 km, Time = 18.9 hours (as 54/60 = 0.9)

**Formula:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed | Speed of boat in still water (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2

 Boat Speed (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2
 

 

 

 
• 
 

 Downstream: x + y (Speed D)
 
• 
 

 Upstream: x − y (Speed U)

⇒ Let 1/D = a and 1/U = b

⇒ 60a + 40b = 12.5 --- (i)

⇒ 84a + 63b = 18.9 --- (ii)

⇒ Multiply (i) by 1.4: 84a + 56b = 17.5

⇒ Subtracting from (ii): (84a + 63b) − (84a + 56b) = 18.9 − 17.5

⇒ 7b = 1.4 ⇒ b = 0.2

⇒ U = 1/b = 1/0.2 = 5 km/h

⇒ 60a + 40(0.2) = 12.5 ⇒ 60a + 8 = 12.5

⇒ 60a = 4.5 ⇒ a = 0.075

⇒ D = 1/a = 1/0.075 = 13.33 km/h

⇒ Speed of boat (x) = (13.33 + 5) ÷ 2 = 18.33 ÷ 2 = 9.165 km/h

⇒ Nearest integer = 9 km/h

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

If speed of boat is x and stream is y, then Downstream (D) = x + y and Upstream (U) = x − y.

Calculating Still Water and Stream Speed

Boat speed in still water x = (D + U) ÷ 2; Speed of stream y = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Time Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. Example: 54 minutes = 54/60 = 0.9 hours.</p
